schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The librarian's graph-tree store, published as a tool nested in the device: deposit, nearest, neighbors, scratch_leaf, the walks, consolidation and the thread helpers over the shared node and embedding tables, plus the vocabulary (NODES, NODES_TABLE, OWNER, RESOLUTION_FLOOR) every tenant names. Every caller outside the librarian reaches the trees through this module and nothing else of the librarian's.
why: RULE 1 (Akien, 2026-10-01): every component talks to every other only through its public interface, and a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes. Measured before the build (encapsulation_breaches, 2026-10-02): 13 rows reached into cairn.devices.librarian.trees and 3 into cairn.devices.librarian.loop for RESOLUTION_FLOOR. The trees ship vectors on every walk, too heavy for a bus round trip per row, so the librarian publishes its store the way db_domain publishes its client (ticket 4cbf6e28126e).
entry: GRAFTED by git mv from cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py, ticket 883abe55d04c, 2026-10-02. The store's bytes moved unchanged; the device class left for cairn/devices/librarian/device.py and RESOLUTION_FLOOR came in from loop.py; every importer's dotted path was rewritten.
invoke: `from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees import trees` (or `from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees import deposit, nearest, NODES, RESOLUTION_FLOOR, ...`). Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py` (exit 0 = green).
state_and_history: A TOOL HOLDS NO STATE OF ITS OWN (Law 6): the shared node and embedding tables are the librarian's, and each tenant's leaf table is the tenant's, gated by the owner CHECK in db_domain's store. Its design history rides the librarian device's history (cairn/devices/librarian/) under ticket 883abe55d04c; nothing beside this charter holds history.
proof: proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py — three teeth, one per falsifier clause of 883abe55d04c: nothing reaches into the librarian for its trees (encapsulation_breaches carries no row on librarian.trees or librarian.loop); the old address is gone (no .py names it, the file is gone, the tool holds no device class); the tool is published (this charter's two fields, its one device import is db_domain's client, its surface, the loop reads its floor, the device class stands in the device). Names resolve late, so a hollow revert reds tooth by tooth.
gates: Import gate — encapsulation_holds in build_inspector (RULE 1, ticket 56d1aff4455e) admits a reach into the librarian only through this tool, because this charter says published_by_device and names its one module. Seal: the tester seals proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py into validations/ beside it.
falsifier: Red if any import outside the librarian lands on librarian code other than cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees, if anything still imports cairn.devices.librarian.trees, or if this charter stops declaring published_by_device and exactly its one module.
learns: It does not; it is the store the graph trees learn ON — deposits, walks and the owner gate are fixed physics, and what learns is the librarian and the tenants that use it.
how_it_learns: It does not; it is the store the graph trees learn ON — deposits, walks and the owner gate are fixed physics, and what learns is the librarian and the tenants that use it.
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation — a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes)
Law 6 (the shared tables are the librarian's, each leaf table its tenant's)
owner: None of its own — a tool has users (Law 6): every component that deposits or walks a graph tree. Its code is held by the librarian, which publishes it; CC gates writes to that code and its proofs.
